q.q: Choose the correct pronoun usage for the following sentence: 'Between you and ___, the new software architecture is significantly more complex than the previous one.'
q.x: The word 'between' is a preposition, and therefore requires an object pronoun. 'Me' is the correct objective case pronoun to follow the preposition.

q.q: Which sentence is in the passive voice?
o: The meal was prepared by the chef.
The chef is preparing the meal.
The chef will prepare the meal.
q.x: Passive voice is characterized by the object becoming the subject of the sentence, accompanied by a form of 'to be' and the past participle. 'The meal was prepared by the chef' follows this structure. All other options are in the active voice.

q.q: Choose the correct verb form to complete the sentence: 'Each of the students _______ submitted their assignment on time.'
q.x: The subject 'Each' is grammatically singular, so it requires a singular verb. Even though 'students' is plural, the prepositional phrase 'of the students' does not change the subject. Therefore, 'has' is the correct choice.

q.q: Fill in the blank with the correct preposition: 'The cat jumped _____ the table.'
q.x: The preposition 'on' is used to indicate movement towards a surface. The cat moving to the top of the table is best described by 'jumped on'. The other prepositions do not fit the motion context.

q.q: Select the option that correctly addresses the dangling modifier in the following sentence: 'Having analyzed the network traffic, the security breach was finally identified by the IT team.'
o: Having analyzed the network traffic, the IT team finally identified the security breach.
The IT team, having analyzed the network traffic, the security breach was identified.
Having been analyzed, the IT team identified the security breach in the network traffic.
The security breach was identified by the IT team, having analyzed the network traffic.
q.x: A dangling modifier occurs when the introductory participle phrase does not logically modify the subject that follows it. In the original sentence, the breach itself did not analyze the traffic. Option 0 correctly places the 'IT team' as the subject performing the action.

q.q: Complete the sentence: 'Neither the teacher nor the students _______ present in the hall.'
q.x: When using 'neither...nor', the verb must agree with the subject closest to it. Since 'students' is plural, the verb must be 'were'.

q.q: Choose the correct sentence to complete the blank: 'She _____ to the library every Saturday morning.'
q.x: The subject 'She' is third-person singular, requiring the verb to have an '-es' suffix in the present simple tense. Therefore, 'goes' is the correct form. Other options do not fit the grammatical structure of the present habitual action.

q.q: Identify the error in the following sentence: 'Hardly had he stepped out of the house when it started to rain.'
q.x: The sentence is actually grammatically correct as written. In many multiple-choice formats, if no error exists, the option representing 'no error' would be selected; however, given the structure, the sentence follows the correct inversion rule for 'Hardly'.

q.q: Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank: 'The project manager was ______ to the suggestions made by the junior developers.'
q.x: The word 'amenable' means open and responsive to suggestion. 'Amendable' refers to something that can be changed or improved, which is incorrect in this context.

q.q: Identify the part of speech of the word 'fast' in the sentence: 'He is a fast runner.'
q.x: In this sentence, 'fast' modifies the noun 'runner'. Therefore, it functions as an adjective.

q.q: Identify the sentence that correctly utilizes the subjunctive mood in a formal context.
o: The board insisted that the CEO resigns immediately to preserve the firm's reputation.
It is imperative that the supervisor be present during the final phase of the audit.
She suggested that he goes to the laboratory to check the server configuration.
I wish that the legacy system was more efficient at handling high-volume data requests.
q.x: The subjunctive mood is required after expressions of necessity, such as 'it is imperative that'. The verb should be in its base form ('be') rather than conjugated. Option 0 and 2 are incorrect because they use indicative mood, and option 3 uses 'was' instead of the subjunctive 'were'.

q.q: Choose the correctly punctuated sentence.
o: I have visited London, Paris, and Rome; however, I prefer Berlin.
I have visited London, Paris and Rome, however I prefer Berlin.
I have visited London Paris and Rome; however I prefer Berlin.
I have visited London, Paris, and Rome, however; I prefer Berlin.
q.x: A semicolon is required before the conjunctive adverb 'however' when it connects two independent clauses. A comma is also typically placed after 'however'.

q.q: Identify the grammatically correct sentence among the following options.
o: Each of the students have submitted their assignment on time.
Each of the students has submitted his assignment on time.
Each of the student has submitted their assignment on time.
Each of the students have submitted his assignment on time.
q.x: The word 'Each' acts as a singular subject, requiring a singular verb 'has'. Additionally, 'Each of' must be followed by a plural noun, making 'students' correct.

q.q: Identify the grammatically correct sentence involving a comparative structure.
o: The processing speed of the new mainframe is faster than the legacy system.
The processing speed of the new mainframe is faster than that of the legacy system.
The processing speed of the new mainframe is more faster than the legacy system.
The processing speed of the new mainframe is as fast if not faster than the legacy system.
q.x: To maintain logical consistency, the comparison must be between similar entities. Comparing a 'speed' to a 'system' is a category error; one must compare the 'speed' to 'that of the legacy system'.

q.q: Complete the conditional sentence: 'If she ______ more time, she would have completed the project.'
q.x: This is a third conditional sentence, which describes an unreal past situation. The structure requires 'had + past participle' in the 'if' clause and 'would have + past participle' in the main clause.

q.q: Select the correct indirect speech form for: He said, 'I will finish this project tomorrow.'
o: He said that he would finish this project tomorrow.
He said that he will finish that project the next day.
He said that he would finish that project the next day.
He said that he would finish that project tomorrow.
q.x: In indirect speech, 'will' changes to 'would', 'this' changes to 'that', and 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day'. All three shifts must be applied correctly.

q.q: Choose the most appropriate preposition to fill the blank: 'He is proficient ______ computer programming and software development.'
q.x: The adjective 'proficient' is typically followed by the preposition 'in' when referring to a skill or field of study.

q.q: Select the word that is correctly spelled.
q.x: The correct spelling of the word meaning a place to stay is 'accommodation', which contains two 'c's and two 'm's.

q.q: Choose the sentence that demonstrates the correct use of a restrictive versus a non-restrictive relative clause.
o: The servers, which were outdated, were replaced last week.
The servers which were outdated were replaced last week.
The servers, that were outdated, were replaced last week.
The servers that were outdated were replaced last week; the newer ones were not.
q.x: A restrictive clause (using 'that') is essential to the meaning and does not take commas. A non-restrictive clause (using 'which') provides extra information and requires commas. Option 3 correctly identifies the specific subset of servers to be replaced.

q.q: Which of the following sentences exhibits correct subject-verb agreement with a collective noun acting as a single unit?
o: The committee of programmers are scheduled to meet at noon to discuss the API migration.
The committee of programmers is scheduled to meet at noon to discuss the API migration.
The committee of programmers have been split on the decision regarding the codebase.
The committee of programmers were in agreement regarding the security protocol.
q.x: When a collective noun acts as a unified body, it takes a singular verb. In option 1, the committee is acting in unison, thus 'is' is appropriate. Options 2 and 3 are less ideal because they imply fragmentation which is not stated.

q.q: Which of the following sentences is grammatically correct?
o: He go to school every day.
He goes to school every day.
He going to school every day.
He gone to school every day.
q.x: The sentence describes a habitual action, requiring the simple present tense. The third-person singular subject 'He' takes the verb form 'goes'.

q.q: Choose the correct pronoun to complete the sentence: 'Between you and _____, I think the plan will succeed.'
q.x: The word 'between' is a preposition, and prepositions must be followed by an object pronoun. 'Me' is the correct object pronoun. Therefore, the phrase 'between you and me' is grammatically correct.

q.q: Choose the correct word to fill in the blank: 'The manager decided to _______ the meeting until next week due to unforeseen circumstances.'
q.x: The phrasal verb 'put off' means to postpone. 'Put out' means to extinguish, 'put away' means to store, and 'put up' refers to construction or accommodation.

q.q: Choose the most appropriate preposition to complete the sentence: 'The committee is divided _______ the issue of new recruitment policies.'
q.x: When discussing a specific topic or matter of debate, the preposition 'on' is standard. 'Divided on' implies a disagreement regarding a particular point.

q.q: Which sentence correctly uses the word 'whom'?
o: The consultant, whom we believed was the expert, left the project.
The consultant, who we believed to be the expert, left the project.
The consultant, whom we believed to be the expert, left the project.
The consultant, who we believed was the expert, left the project.
q.x: In 'whom we believed to be the expert', 'whom' is the object of the infinitive phrase 'to be'. Therefore, the objective case 'whom' is required. Option 1 is wrong because 'was' requires the subject case 'who'.

q.q: Select the correct plural form of 'Child':
q.x: The word 'child' is an irregular noun. The standard plural form of 'child' is 'children'.

q.q: Select the sentence with the correct usage of the correlative conjunctions.
o: Not only did the lead developer write the script, but also documented the process.
Not only the lead developer wrote the script, but he also documented the process.
The lead developer not only wrote the script but also documented the process.
The lead developer not only wrote the script but he also documented the process.
q.x: Correlative conjunctions like 'not only... but also' require parallel structure. In option 2, both parts follow the verb directly, maintaining symmetry in the sentence structure.

q.q: Select the antonym for the word 'Generous'.
q.x: Generous means showing a readiness to give more of something than is strictly necessary. The opposite of this is 'stingy', which means unwilling to give or spend. The other options are synonyms or unrelated.

q.q: Choose the correctly spelled word:
q.x: The correct spelling of the word meaning certain or clear is 'Definite'. The other options are misspellings.

q.q: Select the correct spelling to complete the sentence: 'The committee reached a unanimous _____.'
q.x: The correct spelling of the word meaning a conclusion or resolution is 'decision'. The other options contain common phonetic spelling errors. Accuracy in spelling is vital for professional communication.

q.q: Choose the sentence that correctly uses the semicolon.
o: I have a big test tomorrow; I can't go out tonight.
I have a big test tomorrow; however I can't go out tonight.
I have a big test; tomorrow; I can't go out.
I have a big test tomorrow; and I can't go out.
q.x: A semicolon is used to join two independent clauses that are closely related in thought. Option 0 correctly links two complete sentences without a coordinating conjunction.

q.q: Identify the error in the following sentence: 'The team are practicing their skills for the upcoming tournament.'
q.x: In this context, 'team' is treated as a collective noun acting as a single unit, requiring the singular verb 'is'. Changing 'are' to 'is' corrects the subject-verb agreement error. Therefore, the error is in the phrase 'are practicing'.

q.q: Identify the correct active voice version of: 'The results will have been announced by the board by tomorrow.'
o: The board will announce the results by tomorrow.
The board will be announcing the results by tomorrow.
The board will have announced the results by tomorrow.
The board would have announced the results by tomorrow.
q.x: The sentence is in the future perfect passive voice. To convert it to active voice, the subject 'The board' performs the action in the future perfect tense.

q.q: Select the correct option to fill the blank: 'Neither the CEO nor the board members _______ satisfied with the quarterly report.'
q.x: When using 'neither/nor', the verb should agree with the subject closest to it. Since 'board members' is plural, the verb must be 'were'.

q.q: Which of the following phrases is the correct idiomatic expression for 'to reveal a secret'?
o: To let the cat out of the bag
q.x: Both 'to let the cat out of the bag' and 'to spill the beans' are common English idioms that mean to disclose information that was intended to be kept secret.

q.q: Which of the following sentences uses the past tense correctly?
o: I run to the park yesterday.
I runned to the park yesterday.
I ran to the park yesterday.
I am run to the park yesterday.
q.x: The verb 'run' is an irregular verb. Its past tense form is 'ran', not 'runned'. The other options either use the wrong tense or incorrect auxiliary verbs.

q.q: Identify the sentence that avoids a comma splice error.
o: The firewall was breached, the intruders gained access to the database.
The firewall was breached; consequently, the intruders gained access to the database.
The firewall was breached, consequently the intruders gained access to the database.
The firewall was breached and the intruders gained access to the database.
q.x: A comma splice occurs when two independent clauses are joined only by a comma. Option 1 is a splice. Option 1 uses a semicolon and a conjunctive adverb correctly to join the two independent clauses.

q.q: Select the correct article to fill in the blank: 'It was _______ unique experience to watch the sunrise from the mountain peak.'
q.x: Although 'unique' starts with a vowel letter, it begins with a consonant 'y' sound (/juːˈniːk/). We use 'a' before words starting with a consonant sound.

q.q: Choose the synonym of the word 'Happy' from the given options:
q.x: A synonym is a word with the same or similar meaning. 'Joyful' carries the same meaning as 'Happy'.

q.q: Find the correct synonym for the word 'Prudent' as used in formal business communication.
q.x: Prudent means acting with or showing care and thought for the future. 'Wise' is the closest synonym among the given choices.

q.q: Select the correct passive voice form: 'The technician is repairing the server.'
o: The server is repaired by the technician.
The server was being repaired by the technician.
The server is being repaired by the technician.
The server has been repaired by the technician.
q.x: The original sentence is in present continuous tense. The passive form requires the auxiliary 'is being' followed by the past participle 'repaired'.

q.q: Choose the correct indirect speech form of: He said, "I have been working here for two years."
o: He said that he has been working there for two years.
He said that he had been working here for two years.
He said that he had been working there for two years.
He said that he was working there for two years.
q.x: In indirect speech, the present perfect continuous tense changes to the past perfect continuous. Additionally, the proximal demonstrative 'here' changes to the distal 'there'.

q.q: Identify the error in the following sentence: 'She don't like to play chess in the evening.'
q.x: The subject 'She' is third-person singular, which requires the auxiliary verb 'does not' or 'doesn't'. 'Don't' is used for plural subjects and the pronoun 'I'. Thus, 'don't' is the error.

q.q: Which sentence demonstrates the correct placement of the adverb 'only' to modify the intended word?
o: The software only failed during the high-load testing phase.
The software failed only during the high-load testing phase.
Only the software failed during the high-load testing phase.
The software failed during the only high-load testing phase.
q.x: Adverb placement is crucial for clarity. Placing 'only' before 'during the high-load testing phase' correctly restricts the failure to that specific period, rather than implying the software did nothing else but fail.

q.q: Choose the word that is correctly spelled.
q.x: The correct spelling of the word meaning a room or building for living is 'accommodation', which contains two 'c's and two 'm's.

q.q: Complete the conditional sentence: 'If I _______ you, I would accept the job offer immediately.'
q.x: This is a second conditional sentence expressing a hypothetical situation. In such cases, 'were' is used for all subjects, including first-person singular.

q.q: Select the correct article to fill in the blank: 'He is _____ honest man who always speaks the truth.'
q.x: The word 'honest' begins with a silent 'h', making the phonetic sound a vowel sound. We use the indefinite article 'an' before words starting with a vowel sound. Thus, 'an honest man' is correct.

q.q: Fill in the blank with the correct pronoun: 'The committee members shared _______ opinions during the meeting.'
q.x: In this context, the committee members are acting as individuals with different opinions. Therefore, the plural pronoun 'their' is used.

q.q: Select the sentence that contains a dangling modifier.
o: Walking down the street, the trees looked beautiful.
Having finished his homework, Ravi went out to play.
To succeed in the exam, one must study consistently.
While waiting for the bus, I read a book.
q.x: The phrase 'Walking down the street' is a modifier that logically should describe the person doing the walking, not the trees. Therefore, 'the trees' is the incorrect subject following the modifier, creating a dangling modifier.

q.q: Identify the adjective in the sentence: 'The clever student solved the difficult problem quickly.'
q.x: An adjective modifies or describes a noun. In this sentence, 'clever' describes the noun 'student'. 'Solved' is a verb, 'problem' is a noun, and 'quickly' is an adverb.

q.q: Identify the adjective in the sentence: 'The clever fox jumped over the fence.'
q.x: An adjective is a word that describes a noun. 'Clever' describes the noun 'fox'.

q.q: Identify the sentence that correctly employs the conditional 'would have' structure.
o: If the server had been configured correctly, it would have handled the traffic spike.
If the server would have been configured correctly, it would have handled the traffic spike.
If the server was configured correctly, it would have handled the traffic spike.
If the server had been configured correctly, it would handle the traffic spike.
q.x: In a third conditional sentence, the 'if' clause must use the past perfect ('had been'), and the main clause uses 'would have' + past participle. Mixing these or using 'would have' in the 'if' clause is grammatically incorrect.

q.q: Identify the tense used in the sentence: 'I am reading a book.'
q.x: The sentence uses 'am' + present participle ('reading'), which indicates an action happening at the current moment. This structure defines the Present Continuous tense.

q.q: Which of the following sentences uses the correct article usage?
o: He is a honest man despite his background.
He is an honest man despite his background.
He is the honest man despite his background.
He is honest man despite his background.
q.x: The word 'honest' begins with a silent 'h', making the initial sound a vowel sound. Therefore, the indefinite article 'an' is required before it.

q.q: Complete the sentence with the appropriate preposition: 'He has been living in Delhi _______ five years.'
q.x: We use 'for' to indicate a duration of time. 'Since' is used to specify a starting point in the past. Therefore, 'for' is correct here.

q.q: Select the sentence that correctly uses the past perfect tense to establish sequence.
o: By the time the patch was released, the hackers already stole the data.
By the time the patch was released, the hackers had already stolen the data.
By the time the patch had been released, the hackers already stole the data.
By the time the patch was released, the hackers were already stealing the data.
q.x: The past perfect ('had stolen') is necessary to show that one action (the theft) was completed before another past action (the patch release). Option 1 fails to establish the correct temporal priority.

q.q: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: 'The teacher asked the students to hand _____ their assignments by Friday.'
q.x: The phrasal verb 'hand in' means to submit work or assignments. 'Hand up' or 'hand out' do not convey the meaning of submission in this context. Therefore, 'in' is the correct preposition.
